item.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption considers how universities can manage corruption risks arising from their international student businesses.
item.support: the Commission considers what actions universities in NSW can take in order to manage the corruption risks
item.section: Why the Commission produced this paper

item.text: Its research included university consultations, interviews with more than 40 academics and administrators, and review of relevant legislation and literature.
item.support: More than 40 academics and administrators with significant experience with international students were interviewed

item.text: The Commission identifies tensions between revenue generation and academic standards, alongside risks from market choices and reliance on recruitment agents.
item.support: This creates significant tensions within those universities between generation of revenue and compliance with academic standards.

item.text: The Commission highlights prevention approaches involving market risk assessment, closer oversight of agents and greater separation between recruitment and academic compliance.
item.support: separating the compliance function from the business development function, as feasible

item.quote: This creates significant tensions within those universities between generation of revenue and compliance with academic standards.
